candidates.prompt_text: What game do you like to play or watch? Please say its name and describe it in a few simple sentences.
suggested_ideas: Say the name of the game
Say why it is interesting or fun

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one game and gives a short, clear description of it using simple words and short sentences.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A game is clearly identified; at least one or two basic details are given, such as actions, place, rules, or personal opinion; speech is understandable.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common game is acceptable, including digital games, school games, board games, word games, or sports-related games. The speaker may talk about playing or watching.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about a favorite singer, a school subject, or a holiday with no description of any game.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For PRONUNCIATION, focus on whether individual words and short phrases are easy to understand. Minor grammar mistakes are acceptable if pronunciation remains clear.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not naming a game, giving only one-word answers, speaking too softly, or mispronouncing key words so the game cannot be identified.

candidates.prompt_text: Do you think games with technology and games without technology are similar or different? Give one or two simple examples.
suggested_ideas: Say one way they are similar
Or say one way they are different
Give an example of each kind of game
Say which kind you enjoy more

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker makes one simple comparison between games that use technology and games that do not, with one or two examples.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear idea of similar or different; at least one example; simple supporting detail such as fun, rules, speed, or playing with others.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: The speaker may say they are similar, different, or both. Examples can include video games, quiz games, card games, playground games, or other familiar activities.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Describing a phone model, discussing software in detail, or talking only about school timetables without comparing games.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for clear pronunciation of common comparison words like same, different, easier, faster, and game names. A short answer can still score well if it is easy to understand.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Giving no comparison, listing examples without any link between them, or using unclear pronunciation for key comparison words.

candidates.prompt_text: Think about a simple technology that can be used for games, such as a screen, speakers, or buttons. How does it make a game more interesting?
suggested_ideas: Say what players can see or hear
Say how it changes the game

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one simple technology feature and explains in a basic way how it adds interest to a game.
evaluation_guide.key_points: One technology part is mentioned; one effect is explained, such as sound, color, movement, or quick response; the answer stays simple and relevant.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any basic feature is acceptable, including sound, music, lights, pictures, touch controls, or a timer. The speaker does not need technical knowledge.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Explaining computer programming, discussing the price of devices, or talking about unrelated classroom equipment with no link to games.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For PRONUNCIATION, check whether common words about simple technology and games are articulated clearly. Content can be basic as long as it is understandable and relevant.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Using very general comments with no example, choosing a highly technical explanation, or pronouncing key nouns unclearly so the main idea is hard to follow.
